title: Equity Finance and Debt Finance Overview
context: Review the overview of sources of finance as classified into equity finance and debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital provided by outside investors is an external equity source of finance for the corporation.
Retained earnings that remain in the business count as internal equity finance under the standard overview.
Funds provided by investors are classified as external equity finance in the sources-of-finance framework.
Bank overdrafts and trade credit are commonly listed examples of short-term debt finance.
Long-term bank loans and bonds issued to investors are forms of long-term external debt finance.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Share capital comes from investors outside the firm and counts as external equity finance.
TRUE — Profit kept in the firm supplies internal equity without creating a repayment obligation to creditors.
TRUE — Investor contributions enter as external equity under the textbook classification of finance sources.
TRUE — Overdrafts and supplier credit finance short-term obligations and are grouped as short-term debt.
TRUE — Multi-year loans and bond issues provide longer-term creditor finance that must be serviced.

title: Internal and External Finance Classification
context: Consider a manufacturing corporation that combines share capital from outside investors, retained profits, and a multi-year bank loan to expand production capacity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Equity finance encompasses both internal sources such as retained earnings and external sources such as share capital.
Short-term bank loans used to cover working capital are classified as short-term debt finance.
Debt finance is always external because borrowed funds create obligations to outside creditors.
The balance sheet reveals the sources of finance that a business has used in building its assets.
Large businesses are obliged to draw up a balance sheet showing how operations have been funded.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — The overview treats equity as having internal and external elements, unlike debt which is external.
TRUE — Short-term bank loans finance near-term needs and belong to short-term debt finance.
TRUE — All debt finance is external; creditors lie outside the firm regardless of loan maturity.
TRUE — The balance sheet displays how assets are financed through equity and debt sources.
TRUE — Large firms must prepare a balance sheet under the accounting framework referenced in the chapter.

title: Misclassifying Retained Earnings
context: Review how short-term credit and long-term credit fit within external debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A loan provided by owners is classified as long-term credit within external debt finance.
Share capital is internal equity finance because issued shares are recorded on the corporation's own balance sheet.
Retained earnings are external equity because they ultimately derive from revenue paid by customers.
Debt finance is classified as internal finance because interest payments return profit to the owners.
Bank overdrafts are long-term debt finance because the overdraft limit may remain available for years.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Owner loans appear under long-term credit as external debt, not as equity.
FALSE — Share capital comes from outside investors and is external equity, not internal equity.
FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity even though they originate from trading activity.
FALSE — Debt finance is external; interest is a cost of borrowing, not internal equity.
FALSE — Overdrafts are classified as short-term credit despite renewable facilities.

title: Core Sources of Finance Definitions
context: Analyze the role of the balance sheet in revealing the sources of finance a business has used. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Bonds are short-term debt finance because holders may sell them quickly on secondary markets.
Trade credit from suppliers is short-term debt finance that postpones payment for goods and services.
Bonds issued to investors provide long-term debt finance through formal creditor instruments.
Long-term bank loans are a form of long-term external debt finance used for extended investment periods.
A loan provided by owners is equity finance because owners already participate in business ownership.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Bonds are long-term debt finance even when traded after issue.
TRUE — Supplier credit is a textbook short-term debt source for routine purchases.
TRUE — Bond issues raise long-term external debt from investors who hold creditor status.
TRUE — Multi-year bank loans are listed under long-term credit in the finance overview.
FALSE — Owner loans are long-term credit and debt finance, not equity, despite the owners' stake.

title: Equity and Debt Sources in Practice
context: Consider a construction firm financing payroll gaps with short-term bank loans and supplier trade credit while shareholders provide additional share capital. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Table 3 groups bank overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans under short-term debt finance.
Table 3 includes bank loans, owner loans, and bonds among long-term credit sources.
Retained earnings supply internal equity finance without bringing in new external funds.
Bank overdrafts provide flexible short-term debt finance for day-to-day cash shortfalls.
Share capital and retained earnings both appear as equity finance sources on the balance sheet.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans appear as short-term debt in the overview.
TRUE — Bank loans, owner loans, and bonds are long-term credit examples in the table.
TRUE — Undistributed profit kept in the firm is internal equity, not external borrowing.
TRUE — Overdraft facilities are a standard short-term debt source in the finance table.
TRUE — Equity finance components including share capital and retained earnings fund the balance sheet.

title: Short-Term Debt and Internal Equity
context: Analyze the classification of bank overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans within debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Short-term and long-term credit from creditors are recorded as debt finance on the balance sheet.
Trade credit is equity finance because suppliers effectively share the commercial risk of the buyer.
Funds provided by investors are debt finance because investors expect a financial return.
Retained earnings are debt finance because they must eventually be repaid to creditors.
Equity finance includes share capital from investors and retained earnings kept within the firm.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Creditor funds from short-term and long-term credit appear as debt finance sources.
FALSE — Supplier trade credit is short-term debt finance, not equity shared with suppliers.
FALSE — Investor funds are external equity; expecting a return does not reclassify them as debt.
FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity, not liabilities owed to external creditors.
TRUE — Equity spans external share capital and internal retained earnings in the overview.

title: Balance Sheet and Finance Sources
context: Review long-term debt sources including bank loans, owner loans, and bonds. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Debt finance covers short-term credit such as overdrafts and long-term credit such as bank loans.
Funds provided by investors count as external equity when investors subscribe for ownership in the firm.
Retained earnings reinvested in the business represent internal equity finance rather than borrowed funds.
Short-term bank loans are short-term debt finance used to cover temporary funding gaps.
A loan provided by owners is long-term debt finance even though the lenders are also owners of the firm.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Debt finance is split into short-term and long-term credit categories.
TRUE — Investor contributions are external equity under the sources-of-finance overview.
TRUE — Profit kept in the firm supplies internal equity without interest charges.
TRUE — Short-term bank loans belong to short-term credit in the finance table.
TRUE — Owner loans are long-term credit and remain debt finance despite the owners' equity stake.

title: Long-Term Credit and Bond Finance
context: Consider a freight carrier that mixes short-term credit lines, owner-provided long-term loans, and reinvested earnings to renew its vehicle fleet. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Table 3 shows that debt finance is always external to the business entity.
Table 3 lists share capital, retained earnings, and investor funds under equity finance categories.
Bonds issued to investors are long-term external debt finance creating creditor claims on the business.
Retained earnings are internal equity finance because undistributed profit remains within the business.
Retained earnings become external equity once the firm publishes audited accounts to outside parties.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Debt finance in the table is external; no internal debt category is listed.
TRUE — The table places share capital, retained earnings, and investor funds within equity finance.
TRUE — Bond issues are a textbook long-term debt source funded by outside investors.
TRUE — Retained earnings are reinvested internally and classified as internal equity finance.
FALSE — Retained earnings remain internal equity; external reporting does not reclassify them as external.

title: Owner Loans Versus Share Capital
context: Review Table 3 on the most commonly used sources of finance for businesses. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital is long-term debt finance because shareholders commit funds for many years.
Trade credit from suppliers is short-term external debt finance for purchases on deferred payment terms.
Short-term bank loans are long-term debt finance when the borrower intends to renew them repeatedly.
Debt finance can be internal when the lender is a shareholder who also receives dividend payments.
Share capital from investors is external equity finance contributing to the ownership base of the corporation.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Share capital is external equity, not debt, regardless of how long investors remain.
TRUE — Trade credit is a textbook short-term debt source in the finance overview.
FALSE — Short-term bank loans remain short-term debt regardless of renewal intentions.
FALSE — Debt finance is external even if the creditor is also a shareholder; lending creates debt, not equity.
TRUE — Share capital is external equity from outside investors.

title: Nuanced Debt and Equity Distinctions
context: Consider a software startup that raises share capital from external investors while using retained earnings and short-term bank loans during early growth. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained earnings are external equity because they represent value generated from outside customer payments.
Bonds and long-term bank loans are long-term debt finance creating creditor claims on the firm.
Bank overdrafts are equity finance when used to cover working capital shortfalls.
Table 3 classifies retained earnings as short-term debt because they can be spent within one year.
Equity finance comprises internal retained earnings and external share capital and investor funds.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity even though revenue comes from customers.
TRUE — Bonds and long-term bank loans are long-term external debt.
FALSE — Overdrafts are short-term debt finance, not equity, regardless of working-capital purpose.
FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity finance, not short-term debt.
TRUE — Equity includes internal and external elements in the finance table.

title: Table 3 Finance Sources
context: Review why large businesses are obliged to draw up a balance sheet showing sources of finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Debt finance is external and divided into short-term credit and long-term credit components.
Long-term bank loans, owner loans, and bonds exemplify long-term external debt finance.
Bank overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans exemplify short-term debt finance.
The balance sheet reveals which equity and debt sources have funded the business assets.
Retained earnings are internal equity finance because profit kept in the firm does not come from new external borrowing.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Debt is external with short-term and long-term subdivisions.
TRUE — Bank loans, owner loans, and bonds are long-term debt sources.
TRUE — Overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans are short-term debt.
TRUE — The balance sheet shows the finance sources used by the business.
TRUE — Retained earnings are internal equity from undistributed profit.

title: Single Correct Bond Classification
context: Analyze how a loan provided by owners is classified among long-term credit sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Equity finance is always external because only shareholders provide it.
Trade credit is long-term debt finance because supplier relationships often continue for many years.
Bonds are short-term debt finance because coupon payments occur at regular intervals.
Share capital is external equity finance because investors contribute ownership funds from outside the business.
Share capital is debt finance because investors provide funds that must eventually be repaid with interest.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Equity includes internal retained earnings as well as external share capital.
FALSE — Trade credit is short-term debt despite ongoing supplier relationships.
FALSE — Regular coupon payments do not make bonds short-term debt; bonds are long-term credit.
TRUE — Share capital is external equity from outside investors.
FALSE — Share capital is external equity; equity capital is not repaid like debt with interest.

title: Trade Credit and Overdraft Traps
context: Consider a catering business that covers weekly purchases with supplier credit, reinvests surplus profit internally, and maintains a long-term loan from its owners. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained earnings are external equity because they arise from revenue paid by outside customers.
Bank overdrafts are short-term debt finance even when used repeatedly throughout the trading year.
Bank overdrafts are equity finance when the account holder is also a major shareholder of the bank.
A loan provided by owners is equity finance because the lenders share in the ownership of the business.
Long-term bank loans are long-term external debt finance with scheduled repayment over extended periods.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity despite arising from external trading.
TRUE — Overdrafts remain short-term debt even with repeated use within a year.
FALSE — Overdrafts are short-term debt; the customer's shareholding in the bank does not reclassify the overdraft.
FALSE — Owner loans are long-term credit and debt finance, not equity, despite shared ownership.
TRUE — Long-term bank loans are long-term external debt.

title: Investor Funds Classification
context: Analyze how funds provided by investors are classified relative to internal retained earnings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Funds provided by investors are short-term debt finance when investors expect to exit within one reporting cycle.
Bonds issued to investors are long-term debt finance creating creditor claims traded in capital markets.
Debt finance includes internal sources when the firm repays loans using its own retained earnings.
Share capital is internal equity finance because share registers are maintained within the corporation's offices.
Retained earnings are external equity because they are disclosed in published financial statements.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Investor funds are external equity, not short-term debt, regardless of expected holding period.
TRUE — Bonds are long-term debt from external investors.
FALSE — Using retained earnings to repay loans does not make debt finance internal; debt remains external.
FALSE — Share capital is external equity from outside investors, not internal equity.
FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity; publication in accounts does not make them external.

title: Mixed Finance Source Assertions
context: Analyze how bond issues and bank loans both supply long-term external debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital and funds from investors are external equity finance sources listed in the finance overview.
Retained earnings are internal equity finance sourced from profits not distributed to shareholders.
Bank overdrafts are long-term debt finance because banks review and maintain overdraft limits over time.
Bonds are long-term debt finance raising external creditor funds from investors.
Trade credit is short-term debt finance allowing suppliers to defer cash receipt for goods delivered.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Share capital and investor funds are external equity sources.
TRUE — Retained earnings are internal equity from undistributed profit.
FALSE — Overdrafts are short-term debt despite ongoing bank review of limits.
TRUE — Bonds are long-term external debt from investors.
TRUE — Trade credit is short-term debt from suppliers.

title: Comprehensive Finance Source Review
context: Review how trade credit from suppliers functions as short-term external debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Long-term bank loans are long-term debt finance with repayment schedules extending beyond one year.
A loan provided by owners is long-term credit classified as external debt finance in the overview.
Short-term bank loans are short-term debt finance covering near-term working-capital requirements.
Equity finance includes both internal retained earnings and external share capital from investors.
Debt finance is external and includes short-term credit such as overdrafts and trade credit.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Long-term bank loans are long-term external debt.
TRUE — Owner loans are long-term credit within debt finance.
TRUE — Short-term bank loans are short-term debt for working capital.
TRUE — Equity combines internal and external sources in the finance overview.
TRUE — Debt is external and includes short-term credit categories.

title: External Debt and Equity Boundaries
context: Analyze why equity finance includes both internal and external components whereas debt finance is external. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Trade credit is equity finance because suppliers extend payment terms as a commercial partnership.
Bonds issued to investors are long-term debt finance creating marketable creditor instruments.
Retained earnings are internal equity finance because kept profit funds the business without new borrowing.
Share capital is external equity finance from investors who subscribe for shares in the corporation.
Bank overdrafts are short-term debt finance for bridging temporary cash shortfalls on current accounts.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Trade credit is short-term debt, not equity shared with suppliers.
TRUE — Bonds are long-term external debt finance.
TRUE — Retained earnings are internal equity from kept profit.
TRUE — Share capital is external equity from outside investors.
TRUE — Overdrafts are short-term debt for liquidity needs.

title: Retained Earnings as Internal Equity
context: Review how short-term bank loans differ from long-term bank loans in the finance overview. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Funds provided by investors are external equity finance when investors supply ownership capital to the business.
Bonds are short-term debt finance because issuers may redeem some issues before the final maturity date.
Equity finance and debt finance are both primarily internal because they appear on the firm's balance sheet.
Share capital is long-term debt finance because equity investors commit capital for extended periods.
Retained earnings are debt finance because accumulated profit must eventually be returned to creditors.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Investor contributions are external equity under the sources-of-finance framework.
FALSE — Early redemption options do not reclassify bonds as short-term debt; bonds are long-term credit.
FALSE — Only part of equity is internal; debt finance is entirely external despite balance-sheet presentation.
FALSE — Share capital is external equity, not long-term debt from creditors.
FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity, not debt owed to creditors.

title: Basic Equity and Debt Pairings
context: Analyze how share capital and bonds both involve outside parties yet belong to different finance categories. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained earnings are internal equity finance representing profit reinvested rather than paid to owners.
Share capital is external equity finance contributed by investors who acquire ownership stakes.
Bank overdrafts are equity finance when the firm uses them to protect owner dividends from cash shortfalls.
A loan provided by owners is long-term credit within external debt finance despite the lenders' ownership role.
Bonds and long-term bank loans are long-term debt finance sources from external creditors.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Retained earnings are internal equity from kept profit.
TRUE — Share capital is external equity from investors.
FALSE — Overdrafts are short-term debt finance, not equity, regardless of dividend protection purpose.
TRUE — Owner loans are long-term credit classified as external debt.
TRUE — Bonds and long-term bank loans are long-term external debt.

title: Full Sources-of-Finance Matrix
context: Review how reinvested profit supports internal equity finance without new borrowing. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profit kept inside the firm rather than distributed to owners supplies internal equity finance through retained earnings.
Share capital is external equity finance when investors provide ownership funding from outside the business.
Bank overdrafts are short-term debt finance used to cover temporary cash shortfalls on current accounts.
Long-term bank loans are long-term debt finance with repayment extending beyond the short-term credit category.
Bonds issued to investors are long-term external debt finance listed among long-term credit sources.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Retained earnings are internal equity from undistributed profit.
TRUE — Share capital is external equity from outside investors.
TRUE — Overdrafts are short-term debt for liquidity management.
TRUE — Long-term bank loans are long-term external debt.
TRUE — Bonds are long-term external debt from investors.

title: Investor Equity and Owner Debt
context: Consider a freight carrier that mixes short-term credit lines, owner-provided long-term loans, and reinvested earnings to renew its vehicle fleet. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Funds provided by investors are debt finance because capital injections must eventually be returned to providers.
When investors subscribe for newly issued shares, the resulting share capital counts as external equity finance.
Ownership funding raised by issuing shares to outside parties is classified as external equity finance.
Undistributed profit retained for reinvestment supplies internal equity finance within the business.
Profit kept within the firm rather than paid as dividends represents internal equity finance.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Investor funds are external equity; equity capital is not repaid like debt.
TRUE — Share subscriptions from outside investors supply external equity through share capital.
TRUE — Share issues to external parties raise external equity, not debt.
TRUE — Profit retained rather than distributed is internal equity finance.
TRUE — Dividends foregone in favour of retention create internal equity.

title: Short-Term Versus Long-Term Debt
context: Consider a dental practice that funds routine supplies on trade credit, keeps reinvested profits for equipment, and holds a long-term bank loan for premises. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Short-term bank loans are long-term debt finance when the borrower holds a multi-year banking relationship.
Reinvested earnings that remain inside the business entity count as internal equity finance.
Investor subscriptions for shares supply external equity finance to the corporation.
Retained earnings are external equity because they reflect earnings generated from trading with outside customers.
Share capital is debt finance because shareholders may lose their investment if the corporation fails.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Short-term bank loans remain short-term debt despite a long banking relationship.
TRUE — Earnings kept in the entity are internal equity, not external borrowing.
TRUE — Share subscriptions bring external equity from subscribing investors.
FALSE — Customer-generated revenue does not reclassify retained earnings as external equity.
FALSE — Share capital is external equity; investment risk does not reclassify equity as debt.

title: Isolated Long-Term Bond Source
context: Analyze how owner-provided long-term loans differ from share capital as finance sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Trade credit is long-term debt finance because payment terms may be negotiated repeatedly with suppliers.
Bonds are short-term debt finance because issuers make periodic interest payments to holders.
Bank overdrafts are long-term debt finance because overdraft facilities may continue across several financial years.
Retained earnings are external equity because they are reported to external auditors each year.
A bank overdraft facility on a current account is classified as short-term debt finance.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Trade credit is short-term debt despite repeated negotiation of payment terms.
FALSE — Periodic interest does not make bonds short-term; bonds are long-term debt finance.
FALSE — Overdrafts are short-term debt despite multi-year facilities.
FALSE — External audit reporting does not convert retained earnings from internal to external equity.
TRUE — Current-account overdrafts are short-term debt for liquidity management.

title: Late-Stage Debt Classifications
context: Review how the balance sheet links accounting records to the sources-of-finance overview. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital is internal equity because the shares are recorded on the company's own books.
A loan provided by owners is equity finance because owners reinvest through their existing ownership stake.
Drawing on an agreed overdraft limit to cover cash shortfalls represents short-term debt finance.
Delayed payment to suppliers under trade credit terms qualifies as short-term debt finance.
Supplier credit that postpones cash payment for delivered goods is short-term debt finance.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Share capital is external equity from outside investors, not internal equity.
FALSE — Owner loans are long-term credit and debt finance, not equity reinvestment.
TRUE — Using an overdraft draws on short-term external debt.
TRUE — Deferred supplier payment is short-term debt under trade credit.
TRUE — Postponed supplier payment is short-term debt, not equity.

title: Single Internal Equity Statement
context: Analyze how short-term credit sources support working-capital needs without altering ownership. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Investor funds are debt finance because investors supply capital expecting future returns.
Bank overdrafts are equity finance when used repeatedly to fund the owner's working capital cycle.
Retained earnings are short-term debt because they can be deployed for working capital within one year.
Share capital is short-term debt finance because new shares may be issued to raise quick funds.
Borrowing from a bank for a period of less than one year is short-term debt finance.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Investor funds are external equity; expecting returns classifies them as equity investors, not creditors.
FALSE — Overdrafts are short-term debt finance, not equity, regardless of repeated use.
FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity finance, not short-term debt.
FALSE — Share capital is external equity, not short-term debt from creditors.
TRUE — Sub-one-year bank borrowing is short-term debt finance.

title: Integrated Finance Source Set
context: Review how retained earnings accumulate as internal equity from undistributed profit. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Working-capital bank loans repayable within a year belong to short-term debt finance.
Multi-year borrowing from a commercial bank is long-term debt finance.
Scheduled bank lending with repayment over several years counts as long-term debt finance.
Marketable bonds sold to outside investors are long-term debt finance.
Issuing bonds to raise creditor funds from investors is long-term external debt finance.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Near-term bank loans for working capital are short-term debt.
TRUE — Commercial bank lending over many years is long-term debt.
TRUE — Multi-year scheduled bank loans are long-term external debt.
TRUE — Bonds sold to investors are long-term debt with creditor status.
TRUE — Bond issues raise long-term debt from external investors.

title: Alternating True and False Pattern
context: Consider a neighbourhood bakery that funds daily ingredient purchases through supplier credit while reinvesting part of its annual profit into new ovens. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Owners who lend money to their own firm provide long-term credit classified as external debt finance.
Bonds are equity finance because bondholders participate indirectly in corporate performance through coupons.
A long-term loan from owners appears under long-term credit as external debt finance in the overview.
Trade credit is internal finance because it uses supplier relationships already embedded in operations.
All borrowed funds that must be repaid to creditors constitute external debt finance.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Owner lending creates long-term external debt, not equity.
FALSE — Bonds are long-term external debt; coupon receipts do not make bondholders equity owners.
TRUE — Owner loans sit in long-term credit as external debt.
FALSE — Trade credit is short-term external debt finance, not internal finance.
TRUE — Repayable creditor funds are always external debt.

title: Standard Finance Table Assertions
context: Review why supplier trade credit is grouped with other short-term debt sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Creditor finance obtained from parties outside the business is always classified as debt finance.
The finance overview lists both internal retained earnings and external share capital under equity finance.
Mandatory balance sheets for large firms disclose how equity and debt sources have funded assets.
Large corporations must publish balance sheets showing the sources of finance used to acquire assets.
Table 3 places bank overdrafts among the commonly used short-term credit sources.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Outside creditor funds are debt finance under the overview.
TRUE — Equity in the overview spans internal retention and external share capital.
TRUE — Large-firm balance sheets show equity and debt funding sources.
TRUE — Published balance sheets reveal the finance sources behind assets.
TRUE — Overdrafts appear in Table 3 as short-term credit examples.

title: Bonds Versus Share Capital
context: Analyze how external equity from share capital contrasts with external debt from bond issues. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The overview lists trade credit alongside bank overdrafts as examples of short-term debt finance.
Short-term credit in the overview includes trade credit, overdrafts, and short-term bank loans.
Long-term credit in the overview includes bank loans, loans from owners, and bonds.
Long-term bank loans are short-term debt finance when the first repayment falls due within twelve months.
Internal equity from retained earnings avoids the interest charges that accompany borrowed funds.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Trade credit and overdrafts are paired as short-term debt examples.
TRUE — The short-term credit category covers trade credit, overdrafts, and short-term loans.
TRUE — Long-term credit groups bank loans, owner loans, and bonds together.
FALSE — Long-term bank loans are long-term external debt even when the first instalment is due soon.
TRUE — Retained earnings fund the firm internally without creditor interest.

title: Late Long-Term Debt Focus
context: Review how internal equity from retained earnings avoids interest obligations on borrowed funds. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained earnings are creditor funds because undistributed profit could otherwise be paid to shareholders.
Funds provided by investors are internal equity when the investors are also employees of the firm.
External equity from share capital increases ownership funding without creating creditor claims.
Bondholders hold creditor claims, whereas shareholders hold ownership claims on the corporation.
A renewable overdraft used for seasonal cash management remains short-term debt finance.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Retained earnings are internal equity, not external creditor finance.
FALSE — Investor funds are external equity regardless of whether investors are also employees.
TRUE — Share capital adds external equity without creditor repayment obligations.
TRUE — Bonds create creditor claims distinct from share ownership.
TRUE — Seasonal overdraft use stays within short-term debt classification.

title: Complete True Set With Balance Sheet
context: Analyze how short-term loans from banks differ in maturity from long-term bank loans. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Investor funds used to purchase newly issued shares are external equity finance.
Retained earnings accumulated over several profitable years remain internal equity finance.
Share capital recorded on the balance sheet reflects external equity contributed by investors.
Short-term bank loans arranged to finance inventory purchases are short-term debt finance.
Long-term bank loans matched to factory assets with lengthy useful lives are long-term debt finance.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Purchasing new shares with investor funds is external equity finance.
TRUE — Accumulated retained profit stays internal equity across reporting periods.
TRUE — Balance-sheet share capital represents external equity from investors.
TRUE — Inventory bank loans with near-term repayment are short-term debt.
TRUE — Asset-matched multi-year bank loans are long-term debt.

title: Single Short-Term Debt Example
context: Review how investor funds and share capital both represent external equity injections. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Debt finance is internal when the borrowing firm already holds substantial retained earnings on its balance sheet.
Share capital is external debt finance because investors advance funds before receiving dividend income.
Bank overdrafts are long-term debt finance because the same facility is used repeatedly each quarter.
Bond finance raised for a major expansion project is long-term external debt finance.
Bonds are internal finance because coupon payments are met from the issuer's own operating cash flows.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Holding retained earnings does not convert external debt into internal finance.
FALSE — Share capital is external equity; receiving dividends later does not make investor funds debt.
FALSE — Repeated quarterly use does not convert overdrafts into long-term debt.
TRUE — Expansion bond issues provide long-term external debt.
FALSE — Meeting coupons from operating cash flow does not make bond finance internal; bonds remain external debt.

title: Equity Internal-External Mix
context: Consider a hotel operator that uses retained earnings for refurbishment, a bank overdraft for cash-flow gaps, and bond finance for a new wing. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Owner-provided loans with multi-year repayment schedules are long-term credit within debt finance.
Retained earnings are external equity because they increase when the firm trades with outside customers.
A loan provided by owners is short-term debt finance when repayment is scheduled within one year.
Equity finance and debt finance are both disclosed through the balance sheet of a large business.
Trade credit is long-term debt finance because supplier agreements often span many accounting periods.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Multi-year owner loans are long-term credit, not equity.
FALSE — Retained earnings remain internal equity despite arising from external trading.
FALSE — Owner loans are classified as long-term credit in the overview, not automatically as short-term debt.
TRUE — Large businesses disclose both equity and debt on the balance sheet.
FALSE — Trade credit is short-term debt despite long supplier relationships.

title: Paired Long-Term Debt Sources
context: Review how long-term credit from owners creates repayment obligations distinct from dividends. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital is internal equity because share certificates are held within the corporation's records.
Retained earnings are external equity because auditors verify them in published annual accounts.
Funds from investors and retained earnings are the two broad equity components in the finance overview.
External debt from bonds must be serviced with interest, unlike internal equity from retained earnings.
Share capital is internal equity because the corporation registers the shares on its own books.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Share capital is external equity from outside investors, not internal equity.
FALSE — External audit verification does not convert retained earnings into external equity.
TRUE — Investor funds and retained earnings form the equity pair in the overview.
TRUE — Bond debt carries interest obligations that retained earnings do not.
FALSE — Registering shares internally does not make share capital internal equity.

title: Single External Equity Claim
context: Analyze how overdrafts and trade credit both provide flexible short-term external finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Trade credit for raw materials delivered today but paid for next month is short-term debt finance.
Bank overdrafts are equity finance because they adjust net assets available to shareholders each month.
Trade credit is equity finance because loyal suppliers effectively co-invest in the buyer's stock.
Bonds are short-term debt finance because issuers pay coupons every six months.
Long-term bank loans are short-term debt finance when the bank reviews the loan each year.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Month-end supplier credit for materials is short-term debt.
FALSE — Overdrafts are short-term debt; monthly net-asset effects do not reclassify them as equity.
FALSE — Supplier loyalty does not make trade credit equity; it remains short-term debt.
FALSE — Semi-annual coupons do not make bonds short-term debt; bonds are long-term credit.
FALSE — Annual bank review does not reclassify a multi-year loan as short-term debt.

title: Introductory Finance Classifications
context: Review how the finance overview separates equity sources from short-term and long-term credit. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital, investor funds, and retained earnings together cover the equity side of the finance table.
Bank overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans jointly cover routine short-term funding needs.
Long-term bank loans, owner loans, and bonds jointly fund investments with extended payback periods.
Owner loans are equity finance because owners already receive dividends from the same business.
Short-term bank loans are long-term debt finance when the borrower has used the same bank for decades.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — The equity side spans share capital, investor funds, and retained earnings.
TRUE — Routine short-term needs are met by overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans.
TRUE — Extended investments are funded by long-term bank loans, owner loans, and bonds.
FALSE — Receiving dividends does not turn an owner loan into equity; it remains long-term debt.
FALSE — A long banking relationship does not convert short-term loans into long-term debt.

title: Mid-Level Debt Maturity Traps
context: Analyze how retained earnings remain inside the firm as internal equity rather than creditor funds. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Only equity finance includes an internal source, whereas all debt finance is obtained externally.
Debt finance is internal when repayments are made from cash generated inside the business.
Retained earnings differ from share capital because retention uses past profit while shares bring new investor funds.
Equity finance is wholly external because only outside shareholders can provide ownership funding.
A corporation's balance sheet shows whether assets were financed through equity sources, debt sources, or both.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Internal finance appears only on the equity side; debt is external.
FALSE — Repaying debt from internal cash flow does not make the original borrowing internal finance.
TRUE — Retention uses kept profit; share capital brings new external investor funds.
FALSE — Equity includes internal retained earnings as well as external share capital.
TRUE — The balance sheet reveals equity and/or debt funding of assets.

title: Owner Loan and Retained Earnings
context: Consider a textile producer balancing retained earnings, investor share capital, short-term loans, and long-term bond finance across its balance sheet. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Large businesses must draw up a balance sheet that makes their sources of finance visible to users.
Short-term credit sources leave ownership unchanged while providing temporary external funding.
External equity through share capital dilutes neither creditor claims nor repayment obligations on debt.
Internal equity through retained earnings can fund projects without issuing new shares or new debt.
Retained earnings are debt finance because directors could decide to pay them out as dividends later.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Large firms' balance sheets must show visible finance sources.
TRUE — Short-term credit funds the firm externally without altering ownership.
TRUE — Share capital adds equity without converting debt obligations.
TRUE — Retained earnings can fund projects without new shares or borrowing.
FALSE — Possible future dividends do not reclassify retained earnings as debt finance.

title: Clear Core Definitions Set
context: Analyze how businesses distinguish internal equity finance from external equity and debt sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital is short-term debt finance because shares can be sold quickly on a stock exchange.
Investor funds are internal equity when investors also serve as managers of the corporation.
Bond issues and long-term bank loans both require interest payments to external creditors.
Bank overdrafts are long-term debt finance because the overdraft limit is reviewed annually.
Supplier trade credit is grouped with overdrafts because both finance near-term obligations as short-term debt.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Secondary-market trading does not make share capital short-term debt.
FALSE — Manager-investors still supply external equity when they subscribe for shares.
TRUE — Bonds and long-term bank loans both carry interest owed to creditors.
FALSE — Annual limit review keeps overdrafts in short-term debt, not long-term credit.
TRUE — Trade credit and overdrafts both cover near-term needs as short-term debt.

title: Scattered True Statements
context: Review how short-term credit and long-term credit fit within external debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital from a public share issue is external equity finance under the standard classification.
Trade credit is long-term debt finance because some suppliers deliver goods throughout the year.
Retained earnings from a profitable year kept for expansion are internal equity finance.
A short-term loan from a bank to cover a quarterly tax payment is short-term debt finance.
Bonds are equity finance because rising bond prices reward holders when the firm performs well.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Public share issues raise external equity through share capital.
FALSE — Year-round deliveries do not move trade credit into long-term debt.
TRUE — Profitable-year retention for expansion is internal equity.
TRUE — Quarterly tax coverage via bank loan is short-term debt.
FALSE — Bond price changes do not make bonds equity; bonds remain creditor finance.

title: Working Capital Finance Mix
context: Consider a manufacturing corporation that combines share capital from outside investors, retained profits, and a multi-year bank loan to expand production capacity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A loan provided by owners is short-term debt finance when the owners expect repayment within months.
A ten-year bank loan to purchase production machinery is long-term debt finance.
A bond issue with a fifteen-year maturity is long-term debt finance from external investors.
An owner loan repayable over eight years is long-term credit classified as external debt finance.
Debt finance creates a legal obligation to repay borrowed amounts, unlike retained earnings kept as equity.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Owner loans in the overview are long-term credit, not automatically short-term debt.
TRUE — A ten-year machinery loan is long-term external debt.
TRUE — Fifteen-year bond maturity places the issue in long-term debt.
TRUE — An eight-year owner loan is long-term external debt credit.
TRUE — Debt carries legal repayment duties that retained earnings do not.

title: External Equity and Debt Quartet
context: Review how share capital, retained earnings, and funds from investors relate to equity finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Equity finance from retained earnings is generated inside the firm, whereas share capital is contributed from outside.
Table 3 distinguishes equity finance with internal and external parts from wholly external debt finance.
Funds provided by investors are short-term debt finance when raised to cover a temporary cash shortage.
Retained earnings are external equity because they grow when the firm sells to outside customers.
Share capital is debt finance because failing firms may leave shareholders with no recovery.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Retained earnings are generated internally; share capital comes from outside.
TRUE — Table 3 separates partly internal equity from wholly external debt.
FALSE — Temporary cash shortages funded by share subscriptions are still external equity.
FALSE — Sales to customers do not reclassify retained earnings as external equity.
FALSE — Shareholder loss risk is an equity feature and does not reclassify share capital as debt.

title: Two True Equity Statements
context: Analyze the classification of bank overdrafts, trade credit, and short-term loans within debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The balance sheet links to chapter 6 accounting by showing which finance sources fund recorded assets.
Bank overdrafts are internal finance because the borrowing firm already holds cash in other accounts.
Investor funds and share capital both increase external equity without adding creditor liabilities.
Overdrafts and short-term loans both address liquidity needs classified as short-term external debt.
Owner loans and bonds both appear on the long-term credit side of the debt finance overview.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Balance-sheet finance sources connect to the accounting treatment in chapter 6.
FALSE — Other cash balances do not make overdrafts internal finance.
TRUE — Investor funds and share capital add external equity, not creditor liabilities.
TRUE — Overdrafts and short-term loans both serve liquidity as short-term debt.
TRUE — Owner loans and bonds share the long-term credit side of debt finance.

title: Owner Loan Among Debt Sources
context: Review long-term debt sources including bank loans, owner loans, and bonds. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained earnings appear as internal equity because no outside party supplied the retained profit as a loan.
Share capital appears as external equity because outside investors supplied the subscribed funds.
Trade credit is internal finance because it uses existing supplier relationships within normal operations.
Bonds are internal finance because the issuer services them from internally generated revenue.
Trade credit appears as short-term debt because suppliers extend payment terms rather than ownership rights.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Retained profit was not lent by an outsider and therefore is internal equity.
TRUE — Outside investors supplied subscribed funds, making share capital external equity.
FALSE — Operational supplier links do not make trade credit internal finance.
FALSE — Servicing bonds from revenue does not make bond finance internal.
TRUE — Suppliers grant payment delay as credit, not ownership, making trade credit short-term debt.

title: Finance Source Combination Review
context: Consider an agricultural cooperative that retains part of member profits, accepts funds from new investor-members, and borrows through a long-term bank loan. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Bonds appear as long-term debt because investors lend funds with fixed creditor repayment terms.
Long-term bank loans are equity finance because they support assets that benefit shareholders.
Bank overdrafts appear as short-term debt because they cover immediate cash shortfalls on current accounts.
Short-term bank loans appear as short-term debt because repayment is expected within a relatively brief period.
Long-term bank loans appear as long-term debt because repayment is spread over an extended schedule.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Bond investors lend on creditor terms, placing bonds in long-term debt.
FALSE — Asset benefits to shareholders do not reclassify bank loans as equity.
TRUE — Immediate cash shortfalls on current accounts are covered by overdraft short-term debt.
TRUE — Brief repayment horizons place working-capital bank loans in short-term debt.
TRUE — Extended repayment schedules place multi-year bank loans in long-term debt.

title: Accessible Finance Distinctions
context: Review Table 3 on the most commonly used sources of finance for businesses. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Owner loans are short-term debt finance because owners may demand early repayment in a crisis.
Short-term bank loans are equity finance when used to protect the firm's solvency for owners.
Debt finance is internal when the creditor is also listed as a shareholder in the annual report.
A loan provided by owners appears as long-term credit because owners lend with repayment terms like other creditors.
Retained earnings are short-term debt because they can be spent on wages within the next month.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — Possible early repayment does not automatically make owner loans short-term debt.
FALSE — Protecting solvency with a bank loan still leaves the borrowing classified as short-term debt.
FALSE — A creditor who is also a shareholder still provides debt when lending under a loan contract.
TRUE — Owner lending with creditor repayment terms is long-term credit debt.
FALSE — Spending retention on near-term wages does not make retained earnings short-term debt.

title: Single Owner Loan Classification
context: Analyze how retained earnings differ from share capital as sources of equity finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Funds provided by investors appear as external equity because investors buy ownership rather than creditor instruments.
Retained earnings appear as internal equity because the firm keeps its own undistributed profit for reuse.
Debt finance is external in the overview because every listed debt source involves an outside creditor.
Share capital is long-term debt finance because shareholders may hold shares for many years.
Investor funds are creditor finance because investors expect the business to generate future profits.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Investors buying ownership receive external equity status, not creditor claims.
TRUE — The firm reuses its own kept profit as internal equity.
TRUE — Each listed debt source in the overview involves an outside creditor.
FALSE — Long holding periods do not convert share capital into long-term debt.
FALSE — Expecting future profits accompanies equity investment and does not create creditor status.

title: Three True Core Concepts
context: Consider a dental practice that funds routine supplies on trade credit, keeps reinvested profits for equipment, and holds a long-term bank loan for premises. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Bank overdrafts are long-term debt finance because the facility remains open until the bank closes it.
Equity finance includes an internal component because retained earnings need not be raised from outsiders.
Trade credit is equity finance because suppliers benefit when the buyer sells the supplied goods.
Large businesses are obliged to draw up a balance sheet so users can see equity and debt finance sources.
The sources-of-finance overview in Table 3 is reflected in how large firms report funding on the balance sheet.
tactical_explanations: FALSE — An open facility does not move overdrafts from short-term to long-term debt.
TRUE — Retained earnings need no outsider and therefore give equity an internal component.
FALSE — Supplier benefit from the buyer's sales does not make trade credit equity finance.
TRUE — Obligatory large-firm balance sheets expose equity and debt finance sources to users.
TRUE — Table 3 finance categories are reflected on large firms' balance sheets.

title: Alternating Debt Maturity Cases
context: Analyze how a loan provided by owners is classified among long-term credit sources. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Short-term credit supports working capital while long-term credit supports assets with longer useful lives.
Bonds are short-term debt finance because some bonds mature in less than five years.
Long-term bank loans are short-term debt finance when the first instalment is due next quarter.
Owner loans are equity finance because owners could have injected the same amount as share capital instead.
Funds provided by investors are debt finance because corporations may buy back shares later.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Working capital uses short-term credit; longer-lived assets use long-term credit.
FALSE — Maturity length alone in common examples places bonds in long-term credit in the overview.
FALSE — A near first instalment does not reclassify a multi-year bank loan as short-term debt.
FALSE — Choosing a loan rather than shares creates debt finance, not equity.
FALSE — Possible later buy-backs do not reclassify investor subscriptions as debt finance.

title: Single Investor Equity Statement
context: Review the distinction between short-term credit and long-term credit within debt finance. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Share capital and bonds both involve outside parties, yet share capital is equity and bonds are debt.
Retained earnings are external equity because they are visible to outside readers of the accounts.
Share capital is internal equity because it represents the firm's own issued ownership instruments.
Bank overdrafts are equity finance when the overdraft is fully covered by owner guarantees.
Retained earnings and bank overdrafts differ because retention is internal equity and overdrafts are external debt.
tactical_explanations: TRUE — Outside share capital is equity; outside bonds remain debt despite both involving third parties.
FALSE — Visibility to outside readers does not make retained earnings external equity.
FALSE — Issued ownership instruments from outside investors are external equity, not internal.
FALSE — Owner guarantees do not reclassify overdraft borrowing as equity finance.
TRUE — Retention is internal equity; overdrafts are external debt.
